claims.section: How to tell the explanations apart
claims.sentence: | Explanation | What it says | The signature only it predicts | What the three windows show | |---|---|---|---| | **H1 · Price** | delegation rises with the wage of the work | D's lower bound above +1 pp in all three windows, **and** D keeping its sign and more than half its size on every composition leg testable in that window | The lower bound clears +1 pp in two windows and not in the third; the leg clause fails in every window | | **H2 · Inverse** | the high-wage work is the collaborative work | D's upper bound below −1 pp in all three windows | Not found: D is positive in all three | | **O-A · A persistent difference not shown to clear the margin** | the direction holds in every window; the size is not shown to clear a point in every window | after H1 and H2 fail, all three intervals excluding zero with the same sign | **Declared** | | **H4 · No relation at the margin** | the share does not track the wage by as much as a point | all three intervals inside ±1 pp *and* not all excluding zero with one sign | Not found | | **O-B · No persistent difference** | — | anything else | Not found | | **H3 · Composition, not price** | a declared difference is carried by a mix that travels with wage — the coding family, or the use-case mix | a declared D losing its sign, or more than half its size, on at least one composition leg, in every window in which that leg is testable | **Declared**, on the Computer & Mathematical leg and the within-group leg, each firing in all three windows |

claims.section: Limitations
claims.sentence: **The top quartile's effective size, and the threshold at which the conclusion flips.** Its Kish effective number of tasks is 10.6, 8.9 and 16.4; the two largest software-modification tasks are a quarter to two fifths of its mass; and the third quartile boundary sits on a single computer occupation's wage, so sort order places 5 to 7 percentage points of the top quartile's mass.

claims.section: Limitations
claims.sentence: **The generalisation bound.** Treated as a statement about tasks rather than about these windows' conversations, the design resolves nothing below about 14 to 20 percentage points — twice the largest difference reported here and twenty to thirty times the smallest.

claims.section: Methodology
claims.sentence: Tasks are priced through the shipped O\*NET 20.1 task statements to `release_2025_02_10/wage_data.csv`, joined on the full ten-character O\*NET-SOC code, `MedianSalary` filtered above 100 and divided by 2,080 for an hourly rate.

bindings.value: $208,000 ÷ 2,080 = $100.00/hr is the wage file's top code; the shipped O*NET DB is 20.1 on 2010 O*NET-SOC codes, recoded to 2019 for any grouping; BLS-EP is keyed on SOC-2018

claims.section: Methodology
claims.sentence: Analysis set: the 1,802 / 2,075 / 2,188 named global tasks with a wage and at least one classified collaboration cell — 97.15 / 96.23 / 96.52% of named-task usage mass, on 818,673 / 854,432 / 848,716 classified conversations, Kish effective 94 / 83 / 126 tasks; 805 / 1,079 / 1,056 tasks with a wage and no classified cell and 5 / 12 / 12 with a cell and no wage are dropped, never zeroed.

claims.section: Methodology
claims.sentence: **Models.** D and the composition legs are estimated with the task mix held fixed, on a conversation-level binomial; intervals are two-sided 95% and are lower bounds under within-task dependence, since no clustering unit exists in any release.

claims.section: Methodology
claims.sentence: Every confirmatory quantity is produced twice by two independent code paths; the largest disagreement in D between them is 1.8 × 10⁻¹⁴ points, the bootstrap standard errors are within 0.9% of the closed form, and their intervals cover 95.2–95.3%.

claims.section: Methodology
claims.sentence: **Reproduction of the published numbers first.** Each wave's own five-pattern automation share reproduces at 51.07 / 46.74 / 45.55% (published 49 / 45 / 44% on the all-conversation base), and Anthropic's released regression returns Figure 2.11 exactly (−3.112, partial R² 0.394, N 111).

bindings.value: published 49% / 45% / 44% on the all-conversation base; reproduced 49.0980 / 45.3554 / 44.1569 and 51.0698 / 46.7394 / 45.5456 on the five-classified base

claims.section: What was set in advance
claims.sentence: The confirmatory set was named and counted in advance: **17 confirmatory estimates** — D, Δ_W and the slope in three windows each, leg (a) and leg (b) in three each, leg (e) in two — **of which 8 are the leg tests**, plus **3 exploratory tests** labelled as such.

claims.section: What was set in advance
claims.sentence: The assumed effect and its provenance: a smallest effect of interest of one percentage point on D, chosen so that the rule could fail, with a realised minimum detectable effect of 0.40 / 0.39 / 0.39 points per window at 80% power.

claims.section: What was set in advance
claims.sentence: The separate materiality line for Δ_W — 0.11 to 0.12 points of Δ_W per point of quartile gap — came from the referee's arithmetic on the brief and is reported here as an assumption, not as a realised relation: Δ_W depends on all four quartiles, and the arithmetic holds in one window of three.

claims.section: What was set in advance
claims.sentence: **The quartile rule at the $43.40 wage mass point.** The registered sentence does not say which of the tasks sharing the boundary wage fall in the top quartile; the registered rule was made reproducible by fixing the tie order on (wage, task text), an order-free fractional rule was run beside it, and both declare the same owner.
